newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Jan 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Jan 20.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on Sunday said her government wanted political consensus on major economic issues for smooth functioning of the economy.
The World Health Organisation (WHO) has expressed concern over reports of arsenic contamination in western Bangladesh and stressed comprhensive analysis of the situation.

Opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) leader Prof Badruddoza Chowdhury has termed former President H M Ershad, freed from jail on bail earlier this month, as "Frankestine", and said that the government had let him loose to malign BNP.
Agriculture Minister Begum Matia Chowdhury said on Sunday that the government had no plan to raise the prices of fertiliser.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina said on Sunday that rapid rural development and poverty eradication would get priority in the next five-year development plan.
Drilling of two more gas wells by the British firm Cairns Energy plc in the Bay of Bengal is likely to begin on January 30.
The government on Sunday removed two senior officials of the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) in a major shake up of the country's stock market regulatory body.
